# Brandon Rose — Case Notes, IP Strategy & Career Documentation

## 1. Intellectual Property Rights Analysis

### Key Facts:
- Brandon works at ApartmentCorp, title "Special Projects"
- His boss Marc Menowitz pays for the company Manus subscription
- Brandon also has his OWN personal Manus subscription (BrandonRose2@gmail.com) and personal GitHub (BrandonRose2)
- Brandon works from home on his personal laptop after business hours on personal projects
- He does not charge overtime for this work

### California Labor Code Section 2870 Protection:
- California law protects employee IP developed entirely on own time, without employer equipment/resources, unrelated to employer's business
- Brandon's personal projects meet all criteria:
  - Own time (after hours, at home)
  - Own equipment (personal laptop)
  - Own accounts (personal Manus subscription, personal GitHub)
  - Unrelated to property management (automation consulting for other industries)

### Marc's Own Systems Prove the Separation:
- Marc geofences Brandon — timestamped proof Brandon is HOME when working on personal projects
- Marc records all work communications via ConnectUC/UCConnect — those recordings show work conversations are about ApartmentCorp business, not personal projects
- Separate Manus accounts (company vs. personal)
- Separate GitHub repos with timestamped commits

### California Non-Compete:
- Non-competes are void in California under Business and Professions Code 16600
- Even if Brandon signed one, it's unenforceable
- Brandon can build competing products after leaving

---

## 2. Recording & Documentation Legal Position

### Brandon's Recording Device:
- Brandon has a Disoidoe 136GB magnetic voice recorder (AI recording device) that he keeps on him at all times at the office
- He uses Manus and Claude to transcribe, summarize, and organize recordings into Google Drive with voice profiles for coworkers

### Consent/Awareness Established:
- Brandon asked Marc if the company would expense an AI recording device
- Marc said no
- Brandon told Marc he would "most likely get one on my own"
- Brandon told Marc it would be "very useful for our sit-down meetings in the conference room"
- Marc did NOT object or tell Brandon not to record
- Marc himself wears a Plaud recorder around his neck at all times
- Two coworkers know Brandon has the recorder
- Brandon signed a consent form for Marc's recording system (ConnectUC/UCConnect)

### Legal Analysis (California Two-Party Consent):
- California Penal Code 632 requires all-party consent
- However: Marc's awareness + lack of objection = implied consent argument
- Marc's own use of Plaud establishes workplace norm that recording is acceptable
- Marc cannot claim privacy violation when he's recording the same conversations
- The only gap: Brandon never explicitly confirmed he purchased the device
